verdicts.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: The guide's landing page lists among what readers will learn: "Reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi". The guide also has a dedicated "Reference Terraform State" step.
verdicts.framing_note: The guide index (a separate file from the next-steps page under review) says the same thing, and the reference-state step exists.

verdicts.text: HCL code can be converted to Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated `pulumi convert` CLI reference includes terraform among its supported source languages: "Valid source languages: yaml, terraform, bicep, arm, kubernetes". So Terraform HCL code can be converted into Pulumi programs.

verdicts.text: Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.
verdicts.evidence: L24 is a recap bullet under "You've completed the Pulumi for Terraform Users guide and learned how to:", and it matches the guide's stated learning objectives in _index.md word for word: "Orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together" (L29) and "Orchestration: Managing both tools in unified workflows" (L42). It summarizes what the guide covers rather than making a separate product claim. I couldn't check any product source because the GitHub search hit a rate limit.
verdicts.framing_note: Recap of the guide's own curriculum, identical to the 'What you'll learn' list on the guide's index page.

verdicts.text: `new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves an output from another Pulumi stack.
verdicts.evidence: The API shape is real. The stacks concept docs show `new pulumi.StackReference("acmecorp/infra/other")` followed by `other.getOutput("x")`, and describe `getOutput` as returning "an `Output` wrapping the named output value, or an `Output` wrapping `undefined`" when the output doesn't exist. However, those docs say to use "the fully qualified name of the stack". A bare "core-infra" only resolves within the current project.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The snippet's core stack exports `vpc`, but the app stack reads `getOutput("vpcId")`, so the names don't match. The example also uses a bare stack name instead of the org/project/stack form. requireOutput is the recommended method.

verdicts.text: The `terraform.state.S3Reference` resource (from `@pulumi/terraform`, also referenced as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`) exists and accepts `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/terraform` `state` module has no `S3Reference` class. It only exports invoke functions: `export const getS3Reference ... export const getS3ReferenceOutput` (plus getLocalReference, getRemoteReference and getAzureRMReference). So `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...)` isn't a real API, and `pulumi.terraform.state` doesn't exist in `@pulumi/pulumi` either. The fix is `terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput({bucket, key})`.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The page also calls `.getOutput()` on the reference. That looks like the StackReference API mixed in. The real invoke result exposes `outputs`.

verdicts.text: ### Complex state referencing
verdicts.evidence: The text is just a markdown section heading ("### Complex state referencing"), not a falsifiable assertion. The regex took the capitalized word "Complex" to be an attributed source, but it isn't one.
verdicts.framing_note: False positive from the regex: "Complex" is the first word of a heading, not a named source.

verdicts.text: `terraform.state.S3Reference` exposes a `getOutput` method that returns Terraform state outputs by name.
verdicts.evidence: The generated `state` module in @pulumi/terraform exports only invoke functions, with no `S3Reference` class and no `getOutput` method: "export const getS3Reference: typeof import(\"./getS3Reference\").getS3Reference" (alongside getS3ReferenceOutput, getLocalReference, getRemoteReference and getAzureRMReference). You read S3 state by calling `terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput({...})` and taking `.outputs`, not with `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...).getOutput(name)`.
verdicts.intuition_flag: The code samples look invented: they mix in the StackReference.getOutput pattern and also use `pulumi.terraform.state`, which doesn't exist.

verdicts.text: The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` properties (logging value "DEFAULT").
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-aws Node SDK's generated `aws.ecs.Cluster` example has `configuration: { executeCommandConfiguration: { ..., kmsKeyId: example.arn, logging: "OVERRIDE" } }`, and ClusterArgs accepts `configuration?: inputs.ecs.ClusterConfiguration`. That shows `kmsKeyId` and `logging` both exist. "DEFAULT" is a valid ECS logging value alongside NONE and OVERRIDE, but this session's source only showed OVERRIDE, so the DEFAULT part wasn't confirmed here.

verdicts.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference lists `--from string  Invoke a converter to import the resources`. The migration guide says: "you can use `pulumi import --from terraform` ... Pulumi will import the resources defined in that file into the stack". Terraform-managed resources can also be imported one at a time by resource ID.

verdicts.text: State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi.
verdicts.evidence: Pulumi's Terraform migration guide says you can import existing resources "in the usual way", meaning one at a time with `pulumi import <type> <name> <id>`, or all at once from a .tfstate file. It also says you can "Coexist with resources provisioned by Terraform or CDKTF by referencing a .tfstate file". That supports moving ownership over gradually. A third-party guide (Encore) confirms the approach: import into Pulumi, then `terraform state rm` each resource so the two tools don't both try to own it.
verdicts.framing_note: The claim is about what Pulumi can do. It holds because `pulumi import` works on single resources and Pulumi can read Terraform state while both tools are in use.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Encore recommends splitting ownership at the module or stack boundary, "never per-resource inside one module". So migrating resource-by-resource is technically possible but goes against some best-practice advice.

verdicts.text: The `pulumi import` CLI takes a resource type token, a resource name, and a resource ID, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`.
verdicts.evidence: The auto-generated CLI reference says: "If using the command line args directly, the type token, name, id and optional flags must be provided. For example: pulumi import 'aws:iam/user:User' name id". The example in the claim, `aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, follows the same order: type token, then name, then ID.

verdicts.text: `terraform.state.S3Reference` has a `getOutput("resources")` that returns a filterable array of resources with `type` and `name` properties.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/terraform` SDK has no `S3Reference` class and no `getOutput` method. The `state` module only exports invoke functions (`getS3Reference`, `getRemoteReference`, `getLocalReference`, `getAzureRMReference`). `GetS3ReferenceResult` contains only `readonly outputs: {[key: string]: any}` ("The outputs displayed from Terraform state."), so there is nothing that returns a filterable resource list with `type`/`name`.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi-terraform/contents/sdk/nodejs/state/getS3Reference.ts (and contents listing of sdk/nodejs/state)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The whole page uses `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...)` and `.getOutput(...)` throughout, and that API doesn't exist. The TypeScript examples on this page probably need to be rewritten to use `terraform.state.getS3ReferenceOutput(...).outputs`.

verdicts.text: The migration helper example calls `getOutput("resources")` on a Terraform state reference and treats the result as an array that can be awaited and filtered.
verdicts.evidence: The example does contain this code (L126-127), but the pattern doesn't work against the current SDK. pulumi-terraform's `sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts` exports only the functions `getS3Reference` / `getS3ReferenceOutput` (plus the AzureRM, Local and Remote versions) — there is no `S3Reference` class and no `getOutput` method, so `await ...getOutput("resources")` followed by `.filter()` isn't supported.
verdicts.intuition_flag: Even in the old StackReference-style API, getOutput returns an Output<any>, not a Promise, so awaiting it and calling .filter wouldn't work. Also, Terraform's state 'resources' list isn't an output value.

verdicts.text: A 'Pulumi import API' exists for programmatically importing resources.
verdicts.evidence: L131 is a placeholder code comment ("// Use Pulumi import API to import resources") inside an illustrative stub method that doesn't call anything. It isn't naming a product called the "Pulumi import API." You can import resources programmatically with the `import` resource option or the Automation API's stack import, but GitHub rate limits stopped me from confirming the exact method in source.
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Pulumi import API" isn't a formal product name. Consider naming the real mechanism, such as the Automation API `stack.import()` or the `import` resource option, or put a working call in the stub.

verdicts.text: Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
verdicts.evidence: The Pulumi Policies docs say: "apply them consistently across resources managed by Pulumi IaC, provisioned with Terraform or CloudFormation, or created manually." For Terraform resources, though, this happens only in Audit mode, which "continuously scans resources discovered through Insights Discovery ... including resources created with Terraform". Preventative mode only checks Pulumi stack resources during preview/up.
verdicts.intuition_flag: "Enforce" is too strong for Terraform resources. Policies only audit them through Insights Discovery and can't block Terraform deploys, and the page's validateResource example only runs on Pulumi stacks.

verdicts.text: `@pulumi/policy` exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and `validateResourceOfType` takes a resource class and a callback `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
verdicts.evidence: In pulumi-policy's sdk/nodejs/policy/policy.ts, `export class PolicyPack` is defined, and its doc example shows `import { PolicyPack, validateResourceOfType } from "@pulumi/policy";` along with `validateResourceOfType(aws.s3.Bucket, (bucket, args, reportViolation) => {...})`. That matches the claim: a resource class plus a callback taking (resource, args, reportViolation).
verdicts.framing_note: The output was cut off before the validateResourceOfType definition itself. The signature is confirmed through the SDK's own doc examples, not the function declaration.

verdicts.text: The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property with values like "public-read" and "public-read-write".
verdicts.evidence: The pulumi-aws Node.js SDK class `aws.s3.Bucket` declares `acl: pulumi.Output<string>`, documented as "Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, and `log-delivery-write`." The property is marked "@deprecated acl is deprecated. Use the aws.s3.BucketAcl resource instead."
verdicts.intuition_flag: `acl` is deprecated in favor of `aws.s3.BucketAcl`, so a policy that only checks `bucket.acl` won't catch public ACLs set through a separate BucketAcl resource.

verdicts.text: The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
verdicts.evidence: The Automation API README in pulumi/pulumi calls it "the programmatic interface for driving Pulumi programs without the CLI." It lists use cases such as "Building higher level tools, custom CLIs over pulumi" and "Using pulumi behind a REST or GRPC API", so embedding Pulumi in applications is supported.

verdicts.text: `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` exports `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` accepting `stackName`, `projectName`, and an inline `program` function.
verdicts.evidence: `sdk/nodejs/automation/localWorkspace.ts` defines `static async createOrSelectStack(args: InlineProgramArgs, opts?: LocalWorkspaceOptions): Promise<Stack>`, and its docstring describes it as "utilizing the specified inline Pulumi CLI program". I didn't fetch the `InlineProgramArgs` definition (stackName, projectName, program) because of the file-read cap, but those fields match the documented inline-program pattern.

verdicts.text: `terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible via the `pulumi.terraform.state` namespace when importing from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
verdicts.evidence: The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` index.ts only re-exports `./cmd`, `./config`, `./errors`, `./stack`, `./stackSettings`, `./projectSettings`, `./localWorkspace`, `./workspace`, `./events`, `./remoteStack`, `./remoteWorkspace` and `./tag`. There is no `terraform` namespace in it. Also, pulumi-terraform has no `S3Reference` class. What it provides is the function `getS3Reference` / `getS3ReferenceOutput` in `@pulumi/terraform`'s `state` module (`export const getS3Reference ... from "./getS3Reference"`).
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi/contents/sdk/nodejs/automation/index.ts; gh search code --owner pulumi S3Reference (pulumi/pulumi-terraform:sdk/nodejs/state/index.ts)
verdicts.intuition_flag: The same page has `new terraform.state.S3Reference(...)` at L57, L69, L74, L122 and L248, but that class doesn't exist anywhere in the pulumi-terraform SDK.

verdicts.text: `stack.setConfig("aws:region", { value })` and `stack.up({ onOutput })` are valid Automation API methods, with `up` returning a result with `outputs`.
verdicts.evidence: This matches the Node.js Automation API as I know it: `Stack.setConfig(key: string, value: ConfigValue)` takes `ConfigValue = { value: string; secret?: boolean }`, and `Stack.up(opts?: UpOptions)` accepts `onOutput` and returns a Promise of `UpResult`, which includes `outputs: OutputMap`. I found stack.ts at sdk/nodejs/automation/stack.ts but couldn't read its contents (raw fetch failed, then GitHub rate-limited me), so this rests on API knowledge, not quoted source.
verdicts.source: gh api repos/pulumi/pulumi/contents/sdk/nodejs/automation/stack.ts (file exists; contents not retrievable)

verdicts.text: Component resources can wrap Terraform-backed infrastructure so that developers create resources in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources, leaving multi-tool complexity to the platform team.
verdicts.evidence: This is a capability claim, and it holds. pulumi/pulumi-terraform ships Terraform state-reference functions in every SDK (for example `getS3Reference` in sdk/nodejs/state/getS3Reference.ts, invoked as "terraform:state:getS3Reference"). Their outputs can be read inside a pulumi.ComponentResource, so the Terraform dependency stays hidden from the developers who use the component.
verdicts.source: gh search code --repo pulumi/pulumi-terraform S3Reference; repo:content/docs/iac/get-started/terraform/next-steps.md L239
verdicts.intuition_flag: The code sample next to the claim uses a type `terraform.state.S3Reference` and calls `.getOutput(...)`. The SDK only exports a `getS3Reference` function and a `GetS3ReferenceResult` type, so the sample probably won't compile. That's worth a separate check.

That matches the Node SDK `ComponentResource` constructor order (type, name, args, opts). I fetched sdk/nodejs/resource.ts, but the output was cut off before the ComponentResource constructor, so the exact signature was not quoted from source.
